subject.title: [Bug]: sandbox-browser noVNC clipboard garbles non-Latin-1 characters (CJK, Cyrillic, etc.)

question: Should OpenClaw replace the sandbox-browser x11vnc/Xvfb stack with a UTF-8-capable VNC server, and what security/auth contract must that replacement preserve?
rationale: The bug is source-supported, but the obvious dependency swap touches the browser observer security boundary and a prior candidate PR closed unmerged after VNC auth/exposure concerns.

options.title: Sponsor secure VNC replacement
options.body: Replace x11vnc/Xvfb with a UTF-8-capable server such as TigerVNC only after preserving password fallback, loopback binding, tokenized observer access, CDP readiness, and Docker image contract proof.

options.title: Choose another input path
options.body: Keep the current VNC stack and solve non-Latin text entry through a CDP/IME browser action, accepting that the noVNC clipboard panel itself may remain limited.

options.title: Document unsupported noVNC Unicode paste
options.body: Declare non-Latin noVNC clipboard paste unsupported for now and point users to a different browser text-entry workflow.

recommendation.title: Sponsor secure VNC replacement
recommendation.body: Replace x11vnc/Xvfb with a UTF-8-capable server such as TigerVNC only after preserving password fallback, loopback binding, tokenized observer access, CDP readiness, and Docker image contract proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The sandbox-browser feature introduction and noVNC observer auth/token security history point to steipete as the strongest routing owner for the security-boundary decision.
